record.title: UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
record.summary: Strategy launched by the UAE Government in October 2017 to achieve the objectives of UAE Centennial 2071, rely on AI for all services and data analysis by 2031, raise government performance, lead the world in government AI investment and create a new high-value market. It targets transport, health, space, renewable energy, water, technology, education, environment and traffic. Its five themes: an AI council and task forces; programmes across government; training of government leaders and staff; delivering all first-line public services through AI; and leadership through an AI advisory council, a government law on the safe use of AI and a first global document on controls for its safe use.
record.notes: Launched in October 2017 as the post-mobile government phase; it sets 2031 as the target year for relying on AI for all services and data analysis. The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence (AE-02, 2024) states that it aims to achieve the strategic goals of this strategy.
record.scope_note: Mainly a strategy for AI adoption in government services and economic sectors; included as the UAE's flagship AI strategy, whose fifth theme provides for a government law on the safe use of AI and controls for its safe use.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: the UAE Government portal (u.ae) page on the strategy in English (snapshot of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged on 18 Oct 2026; last updated 30 Dec 2024) and in Arabic (18 Oct 2026; last updated 30 Jun 2026). They confirm the October 2017 launch by the UAE Government, the aims (the Arabic page adds 100% reliance on AI in services and data analysis by 2031), the sectors and the five themes, and name the strategy 'UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence' / 'استراتيجية الإمارات للذكاء الاصطناعي'. The English page is shorter and omits the 2031 target and, in the fifth theme, the advisory council and the global document on safe-use controls; the summary follows the fuller Arabic page. The English page links the strategy's name to the strategy document on the AI Office's site (ai.gov.ae, file UAE-National-Strategy-for-Artificial-Intelligence-2031.pdf), the source of the previous title 'UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031', the previous original title and the eight objectives of the previous summary; ai.gov.ae refused the archiver again on 18 Oct 2026 (HTTP 403, also in a browser), so that document is not stored.

judgment.status_reasoning: A government strategy launched in October 2017 and still presented as current on the UAE Government portal (page updated 30 Dec 2024); nothing stored replaces or withdraws it. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A national AI strategy whose main content is AI adoption across government and economic sectors; its risk-governance content is the planned government law on the safe use of AI (and, in the strategy document, an objective on governance and regulation). In with a scope_note, as for other adoption-focused national strategies (VN-01, AZ-01).
judgment.date_reasoning: The portal gives only the month of launch, October 2017; 2017-10 is kept.
judgment.topics_reasoning: public-sector use is supported (government services through AI, training of government leaders and staff). international cooperation rests in part on the fifth theme's 'first global document' setting controls for safe use, and accountability & liability on nothing stored; both came from Objective 8 of the strategy document (governance, regulation, an intergovernmental framework), which could not be stored. Left unchanged as the coordinator asked; see open_questions.

open_questions: The strategy document (ai.gov.ae PDF linked from the u.ae page) cannot be stored: ai.gov.ae refuses the archiver, also in a browser. Whether the record should carry its title 'UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031' instead of the portal's 'UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence' needs that document; a person who has the PDF could provide it.

safety_topics: 'accountability & liability' is supported by no stored source and 'international cooperation' only weakly (the fifth theme's 'first global document' on controls for safe use); both rest on Objective 8 of the unstored strategy document. They are left unchanged.
